description:
Scope: planning only for lib/zaq/engine/history_ingress.ex uncovered lines 39,121,143,181,204,206,244,283,302,325,326,390,391,395,429,430,442,443,444,445. Exclusive test ownership: edit ONLY test/zaq/engine/history_ingress_test.exs; do not create other test files or alter production code to inflate coverage. No E2E: this is an existing Engine persistence/error contract, not a new UX feature. No executable Action is added/changed; Action reuse gate not applicable. Follow AGENTS.md, docs/agent-tools.md, docs/testing-approach.md, docs/WORKFLOW_AGENT.md, docs/exec-plans/PLAN_STRATEGY.md, docs/services/engine.md. Recheck the current checkout, line numbers, existing tickets, and coverage before implementation.

Test design/fixtures: retain existing Zaq.DataCase async: false, Oban.Testing repo: Zaq.Repo, ExUnitProperties, connector/1, author/4, capture_delivered/1; construct Incoming.new/1 with explicit provider, source_scope, channel_config_id, conversation_type and participant evidence; create valid recipients via author/4 and real People APIs. Use Repo plus Message/Transcript/TranscriptMessage and all_enqueued/refute_enqueued to check persistence, identity, fixed targets and transactional rollback. A local helper for a confirmed replicated delivery with explicit overrides is justified only if repeated setup makes scenarios clearer; keep decisive bad fields visible. Reuse existing sandbox and Oban testing mode; no external provider/network, live adapter, sleeps, time-based polling, global application env mutation, arbitrary process names or blanket Mox. The injectable resolver for capture can be a tiny test-local deterministic module for resolve/2 and resolve_audience/2; verify on public return and DB state, not private call counts. Real People/Repo/Oban are preferable to mocks. Since file already async: false and owns DB/Oban tests, keep all scenarios there; any unavoidable global Oban config mutation would require on_exit restoration and explicit rationale, but avoid it.

Scenarios mapped to lines:
1) 39,121: assert capture(non-Incoming), capture(%{}, non-list opts), and capture_resolved(non-Incoming, valid id, :channel) or capture_resolved(valid Incoming, nil/0 id, :channel) return {:error, :invalid_request}; no Message/Transcript/TranscriptMessage. Preserve default-argument coverage but do not mistake invalid structs for externally authenticated events.
2) 143: create a valid scoped shared Incoming whose audience.participants includes one linked author and one unknown identifier, with valid context, and capture with resolved author. Assert stored message history_context retains sender participant and excludes unresolved identifier; no Person auto-created by history_context. Note direct capture uses IdentityResolver and falls back to author-only participants without explicit audience.
3) 181: associate_confirmation(invalid UUID) yields Ecto.UUID.cast error branch (line 180), and well-formed nonexistent UUID or existing Message without both metadata keys yields {:error, :missing_confirmation} (line 181). Assert no transcript association/enqueue. Also distinguish disabled/wrong connector active_confirmation_scope returning :invalid_delivery_scope, not missing.
4) 204,206: table of :confirmed with missing provider, nonbinary provider, zero/missing config ID, or unsupported kind => {:error, :invalid_delivery_scope}; unconfirmed/missing confirmation => {:error, :unconfirmed_delivery}. Assert no writes/jobs. Avoid putting unspecified malformed maps into deeper valid guard path.
5) 283: confirmed_delivery?/1 with otherwise valid reference and assistant_message_id set to non-UUID binary must enter confirmed_message UUID-cast fallback and return {:ok, false}; real enabled retrieval connector required. If this call does not reach fallback because input uses a different coordinate branch, verify via public record_confirmation with valid top-level guard and explicit bad assistant ID, expecting scoped error and no persisted artifacts.
6) 302: attempt a valid-guard confirmed replicated delivery with neither binary assistant_message_id nor binary message_id; require transaction to reach confirmed_message(_) while source-lock tolerates missing external ID, then expect a controlled error/no persisted rows. If downstream fingerprint/preparation crashes rather than returning a tuple, do not assert invented behavior: document that 302 is only reachable via malformed internal payload that violates the trusted Channels normalization contract and request owner decision before changing production or adding a test-only seam.
7) 325,326: distinguish a pre-existing Message with delivery_confirmation receipt but no history_association, sourced to the same connector/scope/external ID and suitable valid target response. Matching receipt should pass line 325 and persist fingerprint/targets; differing receipt (e.g. changed channel_id while preserving source coordinates) should roll back :conflicting_delivery_confirmation at 326, leaving original metadata/targets/Oban jobs untouched. Try public execution-answer preparation with real Conversations.admit_incoming/finalize_incoming, or existing canonical Message changeset if permitted; verify that TranscriptHistory.prepare_execution_response binding and source uniqueness do not short-circuit before receipt check. If no legitimate state can reach these branches, mark as legacy-state-only rather than injecting private calls.
8) 390: confirmed replicated delivery with valid Audience and target among recipients and nonempty scope, linked recipient, but invalid Facts.new coordinate (e.g. blank channel_id is impossible while it is in normalized audience; instead an over-255-byte conversation_id/provider or invalid kind as reachable after guard) must propagate {:error, :invalid_history_facts}, roll back recipients/message/targets/job. Prove predicate order so it genuinely enters delivery_facts/2 rather than line 391. 391: invalid audience, delivery channel absent from audience.recipients, or blank source_scope => {:error, :invalid_recipient_evidence} and zero durable writes/jobs. 395: valid top-level kind :channel/:direct with no %Message{} response or missing binary user_message_id => {:error, :invalid_delivery_scope}; commit nothing. If preflight fails earlier, record actual reachable branch rather than forcing invalid state.
9) 429: create linked recipient, update its Person status to inactive using People.update_person/2 or established Ecto changeset, then confirm delivery to inactive plus active recipient; inactive resolves but yields nil, is not a transcript owner, active receives one fixed target. If only inactive, expect :no_linked_recipient and transaction rollback/no job. Check whether People discovery reactivates or rejects inactive before asserting branch; document if public path cannot return {:ok, inactive}.
10) 430: use an actual People.find_or_create_from_channel error path, such as contradictory canonical email owner and channel-link owner for the same recipient within the same connector, while another earlier recipient may have been newly discovered. Assert {:error, :unresolved_history_recipient} and transaction rollback of any newly created Person/links, Message, Transcript and job. First establish the conflicting fixture with existing People APIs and confirm the error is returned (not raised or silently matched). Do not monkeypatch People or introduce a production-only failure seam.
11) 442-445: capture valid incoming with attachments including map/Record carrying nonnil id/name/mime_type/size and another sparse attachment; assert stored canonical attachment descriptors have string keys and exact nonnil values, absent nil keys; no unrelated keys. Incoming.new normalizes attachments; if it discards nil/sparse input, use legal Record instances and investigate supported constructor, not forged private calls. This drives Enum.reduce, nil and value arms.
12) 244: force HistoryDeliveryWorker.enqueue/1 to return non-ok only through existing supported test infrastructure (Oban testing config/unique job constraint or a controlled real DB failure that does not abort the enclosing PostgreSQL transaction before Repo.rollback). Assert {:error, :history_capture_unavailable}, no message/target/job, and a successful later retry. Do NOT modify global Oban state, introduce test-only injection into HistoryIngress, mock static Oban, or corrupt shared DB. If no safe non-ok return is possible, explicitly flag line 244 as unreachable through public supported seam and seek owner approval for a production-meaningful injection or justified coverage exception.

Property assessment: existing bounded ExUnitProperties replay property at lines 885-936 exercises idempotence over body and 1..4 retries; preserve it. Add a small bounded property only if new normalization/attachment/fingerprint invariant spans broad legal inputs and provides information beyond explicit boundary cases (e.g. varying nonnil attachment fields always preserve descriptors and drop nil). Do not make DB-heavy generated cases just to count lines; deterministic examples suffice for invalid guards/error precedence. Keep generated identifiers unique and state isolated.

Validation for implementer, not this planning pass: test-first scenarios, run `mix test test/zaq/engine/history_ingress_test.exs` (plus any directly impacted isolated engine suite), `mix q` after the issue, review diff, then regenerate fresh coverage via coverage phase's `mix coveralls.json`/`mix coverup` and inspect these exact lines; document excluded/unreachable lines with evidence. Final `mix precommit` only at the workflow's final approval gate. Do not run new feature E2E. Record observed branch reachability and coverage-phase exception in Beadwork; keep no test-only production affordance.

comments.text: Correction to scenario 5 (authoritative): confirmed_delivery?/1 executes Map.take(reference, [:provider, :channel_config_id, :source_scope, :message_id]) BEFORE confirmed_message/1, so a supplied assistant_message_id is stripped; it cannot hit line 283. To reach line 283 use public record_confirmation/1 with a valid top-level confirmed direct/channel/replicated delivery and a non-UUID binary assistant_message_id. Confirm that the path arrives at confirmed_message/1, then flows into prepare_delivery and returns a controlled error (typically invalid_delivery_scope for direct/channel) with no durable artifacts. Do not use confirmed_delivery?/1 to claim coverage of line 283. Scenario 302 can use a valid-guard replicated delivery with neither binary assistant_message_id nor binary message_id; confirm the actual downstream return/rollback instead of presupposing it. Scenario 390: invalid conversation_id (>255 bytes) with otherwise valid replicated delivery is the preferred Facts.new error input; top-level kind invalid cannot enter the guarded record_confirmation/1 clause.

Implemented public-contract tests in test/zaq/engine/history_ingress_test.exs: invalid capture requests/no writes; history_context participant filtering/no unknown Person creation; confirmation guard and UUID/missing-receipt errors; canonical Record attachment descriptor output including nil omission. Isolated target suite passed under required fcntl lock. Blocked/not covered here: further planned edge cases (especially enqueue non-ok line 244, malformed internal line 302, and legacy receipt branches 325-326); require reachability work/coverage handoff, no production seam or forced internal contracts used.

Follow-up implementation findings (2026-10-07): added passing public tests for record_confirmation assistant_message_id non-UUID (actual {:error, :source_conflict}, line 283 cast fallback); replicated conversation_id >255 => :invalid_history_facts (390); channel absent from normalized audience => :invalid_recipient_evidence (391); direct confirmation with missing response => :invalid_delivery_scope (395); inactive recipient excluded while active recipient gets the confirmed target (429); missing both assistant_message_id/message_id returns controlled :invalid_delivery_scope through public record_confirmation (302). Targeted suite: 1 property, 23 tests, 0 failures, serialized under required lock.

Reachability evidence/blockers: line 430 contradictory owner setup cannot be arranged through People.add_channel: the API rejects second ownership immediately with unique constraint person_identities_platform_authority_identifier_index; HistoryIngress recipient discovery supplies only normalized channel identity (not contradictory canonical email fields), so its discovery error cannot be driven by that fixture via the public path. Lines 325/326 legacy-receipt fixture attempt used a real admitted/finalized response and receipt metadata, but record_confirmation returned :source_conflict inside TranscriptHistory.matches_admitted_source?/4 before the receipt comparison; no safe fixture reached receipt clauses. Line 244 remains unsupported as previously planned. Do not force those internal states or add seams.

Review correction: unknown participant test now uses supported :to audience role, explicitly proves Incoming.new retains the unknown participant, asserts exact known sender context remains, and verifies no PersonChannel for the connector/identity plus unchanged Person and PersonChannel counts. Isolated target rerun passed (1 property, 23 tests, 0 failures) under the required fcntl lock.
